name: HAITI

flag.title: Haitian Flag
flag.note: Blue over red, coat of arms at centre

lead: Haiti was the first country built by people who freed themselves from slavery. In 1804 Haitians beat Napoleon's armies and declared independence. About 12 million people live among rugged mountains and bright blue sea.
geo: Haiti is one of the most mountainous countries in the Caribbean. Its Taíno name Ayiti means 'land of high mountains'. Farmers grow coffee and mangoes on terraced hillsides.
Haiti shares the island of Hispaniola with the Dominican Republic. Two peninsulas jut into the sea, giving it one of the region's longest coastlines.
animals: The Hispaniolan solenodon has a long nose and injects venom through a groove in its tooth. Almost no other mammal can do that.
The rhinoceros iguana has bony bumps like a horn on its nose. The bright-green Hispaniolan Amazon parrot chatters loudly in mountain forests.
culture: Craftspeople in Jacmel make giant papier-mâché masks of dragons, pigs and politicians for Kanaval. Artists hammer old oil drums into iron sculptures, a tradition begun by blacksmith Georges Liautaud.
Vodou is Haiti's spiritual heart. It comes from West African tradition. During Lent, rara music fills the streets with bamboo horns called vaksen, bells and drums.
history: In 1791 enslaved people on the French colony of Saint-Domingue rose up. Led by Toussaint Louverture and others, they fought French, Spanish and British armies for 13 years.
On 1 January 1804 Dessalines declared the Republic of Haiti. It was the first free Black nation and the first Latin American country to win independence.
wows: Haiti made half of Europe's sugar and coffee in the 1750s.
Haiti finished paying France 150 million gold francs in 1947.
The Citadelle Laferrière is the Americas' largest fortress.
Haiti's flag began when Dessalines ripped the white from a French tricolour.
The solenodon's venom trick is 76 million years old.
Every tap-tap bus is painted with saints and footballers.
Haitian Creole was created in one or two generations.

myths.myth: Nobody lived in Haiti before Columbus
myths.fact: Taíno people had lived there for hundreds of years. In 1492 Columbus's ship ran aground off Haiti's north coast.
Followers believe in one creator, Bondye. Helper spirits called lwa guide daily life. Pin-stuck dolls come from movies.
